item.title: When Nothing Happens Is Actually Something: The Hidden Drama of Trivial Insulators
item.description: Two trivial insulators, each with displaced Wannier centers, host a conformal QED₃ state at their boundary where the energy gap closes.

item.title: When Numbers Become Strangers: Three Erdős Conjectures Fall to Probability
item.description: A unified probabilistic method has toppled three of Erdős's long-standing conjectures on the behavior of prime factors in consecutive integers.

item.title: Weaving Space from Arrows: The Homotopy of Directed Graphs
item.description: Directed graphs, when interpreted through cubical homotopy, encode all topological shapes, from spheres to tori, in their arrow networks.

item.title: The Geometry of Shells: How Three Parameters Capture Nature's Spiral
item.description: Three parameters—a scalar, a vector, and a curve—mathematically generate the spiral geometry of nearly all molluscan shells.

item.title: The Singularity That Wasn’t a Black Hole: Penrose’s 1965 Theorem Revisited
item.description: Penrose's 1965 theorem proves geodesic incompleteness, not necessarily black holes; cosmic censorship conjectures are required to bridge the gap.

item.title: When Noise's Memory Becomes Its Undoing
item.description: In an NMR quantum processor, the Petz recovery map turns noise's own memory into a tailored undo operation, achieving high fidelity when the reference state matches the channel's fixed point.

item.title: When Swimming Helps You Disappear: How Marine Organisms Mask Their Scent
item.description: By stirring the water as they swim, marine organisms like fish can rapidly dilute their scent, becoming undetectable to distant predators.

item.title: A World That Refuses to Shine: JWST Reveals a Planet’s Blank Face
item.description: JWST’s mid-infrared spectrum of LHS 3844 b reveals a dark, space-weathered basaltic surface and no detectable atmosphere.

item.title: The Traffic Jam Inside Your Neurons
item.description: Mitochondrial traffic jams inside axons are caused by spherical mitochondria that tumble and block passage, while elongated ones glide smoothly through.

item.title: When Identical Noise Becomes a Signal
item.description: By forcing identical random number streams across scenarios, common random numbers transform stochastic noise into a precise signal in agent-based simulations.

item.title: When Better AI No Longer Means Better Models of Vision
item.description: As artificial vision models surpass human-level accuracy, their internal representations diverge from the primate brain's visual pathways, breaking a decade-long alignment.

item.title: When Brain Models See Movies but Miss the Story
item.description: Brain encoding models predict neural activity from movies, yet fail to grasp the story, revealing the gap between surface patterns and semantic understanding.

item.title: When a Language Model Learns to Derive Gravity
item.description: An AI apprentice carves cosmic perturbation equations into a stone of spacetime, learning gravity through worked examples and algebra.

item.title: Reading Bodies, Missing Minds: AI’s Struggle with Theory of Mind
item.description: AI can recognize a smile but misses the mind behind it, exposing a gap between textbook knowledge and real-time social understanding.

item.title: A Bar Born Where None Should Be
item.description: A stellar bar, over 7 kiloparsecs long, is revealed in the gas-rich galaxy GN20 just 1.5 billion years after the Big Bang, challenging theories of bar formation.

item.title: Quantum Compressed Sensing: Banishing the Logarithm
item.description: A single quantum probe, through domain-alignment evolution, directly maps sparse signal components to measurements, eliminating the logarithmic overhead of classical compressed sensing.

item.title: Breaking the Monotony: How Thermodynamic Networks Learn to Compute
item.description: By settling into a steady state, a thermodynamic network computes without clocks or logic gates, using negative differential conductance to break monotonic constraints.

item.title: Is Quantum Chaos Hiding in the Second Moment?
item.description: In a many-body spin chain, the variance of entanglement across measurement histories separates chaotic dynamics from integrable ones, unmasking quantum chaos where averages fail.

item.title: Learning to Differentiate: The First Theorem for Operators
item.description: A neural network learns not only an operator but also its Fréchet derivatives, bridging infinite-dimensional spaces with mathematical guarantees.

item.title: A Differentiable Measure That Sees Groups
item.description: A differentiable loss function detects algebraic group structure: its global minimum exists if and only if the data table is isotopic to a group.

item.title: Proving Transformers Are Inherently Succinct
item.description: A compact transformer, no larger than a haiku, can describe patterns that would require a universe-sized recurrent network to match.

item.title: Fluid Dynamics Learns to Intersect: A Geometric Reformulation
item.description: Fluid dynamics is revealed as the intersection of a coisotropic submanifold (spacetime constraints) and a Lagrangian submanifold (fluid equation of state) in an infinite-dimensional symplectic geometry.

item.title: When the Patient's Words Change the Diagnosis
item.description: Benign variations in patient language can shift AI diagnostic outputs, revealing a fundamental challenge for trustworthy medical AI.

item.title: When Optimization Becomes a Mountain: A New Way to Climb
item.description: A new algorithm climbs the complex, quartic landscape of financial optimization by following the affine-normal direction, not just the gradient.

item.title: Spinning Out of the Blue: AI Finds Chiral Superconductivity
item.description: A self-attention neural network discovers chiral p+ip superconductivity by minimizing energy from raw electron coordinates, revealing emergent topological order.

item.title: When a Quantum String Breaks Itself
item.description: For the first time, a trapped-ion quantum simulator observes non-abelian string breaking, where the force that binds quarks tears itself apart without any dynamical matter.

item.title: The Imaginary Distance Bound: When Wormholes Draw a Line
item.description: Wormholes in quantum gravity impose an imaginary distance bound, limiting how far a theory's parameters can be twisted before consistency breaks down.

item.title: Learning a Quantum System's Rules at Any Temperature
item.description: A flat polynomial approximation enables learning a quantum Hamiltonian from thermal states at any constant temperature.

item.title: Compress and Reverse: Making AI Behaviors Reversible on Command
item.description: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) induces new behaviors in large language models, yet imposes no structural constraint on how these behaviors are distributed within the model. Existing behavior interpretation methods, such as circuit attribution approaches, identify spar...

item.title: A Ghost in the Machine: Can Rydberg Atoms Sniff Out Dark Photons?
item.description: A tabletop array of laser-trapped Rydberg atoms could serve as a receiver for the faint electric fields of dark photons.
